cues.text: Thank you for joining me for this brief
tutorial focused on managing pipette
calibration schedules to be used with
the PCS in the ArtelWare application.
I've got some details to share with you.
So, let's go ahead and get started.
Prior to adding a pipette schedule in
ArtelWare, several other tasks should
have been completed before now. Adding a
user, adding a location, adding a
device, namely a pipette, and creating a
calibration plan. If you haven't
performed these steps, go ahead and go
back and do them now. But if you have
performed these steps, let's go ahead
and talk about how you create a pipette
calibration schedule within the Art
Telware application. Now, there's a
couple of different steps to adding a
schedule for a pipette in ArtelWare. The
first is creating a schedule using the
create schedule shortcut on the get
started bar.
The second is by navigating to the
configuration icon on the far left panel
and going to the schedule section. But
for today, let's go ahead and use the
create schedule icon in the get started
bar. The moment I select create
schedule, I'll then be asked to indicate
what type of schedule I'm creating. So
today I'm creating a pipette calibration
schedule. So I'll go ahead and click
okay. Now the schedule name can be
anything that you desire. It's important
to note that typically there's one or
maybe two master schedules that contain
all of the pipettes in any one particular
facility. There usually isn't a need to
have multiple schedules that all have to
deal with pipette calibrations unless
you're performing interim verification
checks or routine checks as well as a
full pipette calibration. In this case,
I'm going to add a semiannual
calibration because I calibrate my pipe
heads every six months. Now, the name is
the only required field in this case.
The description is optional. The type
will automatically default to pipe hit
calibration because that's what I had
selected on one of those first screens
from the get started shortcut. The next
thing I need to consider is how often do
I want this particular interval to
repeat. Now, since this is a semiannual
pipette calibration, I'm going to have it
repeat intervals every 6 months. Next, I
have a choice of do I want that interval
to repeat from its completion date,
which is the date of the actual
calibration, or do I want it to repeat
from a due date. So, a very specific
thing to note in this particular case,
if I select from due date, you'll notice
that the date on the bottom of the
artell application says July 8th. If I
select from due date, that means this
pipette will always be due every July 8th
and every February 8th, regardless of
when the actual calibrations occurred.
So again, selecting the due date radio
button means that your pipette will always
be due on that date, regardless of when
it was last calibrated. So I'm going to
select from completion date because I
want this schedule to repeat from the
actual calibration date of the pipette.
So next we need to add some information.
We need to add the pipettes and their
calibration plan. So I'll click on the
plus sign. From here I'm shown a few
different options. Now typically you're
probably going to have a much larger
list than I do. And if that's the case,
you have these very helpful filter icons
that help you quickly filter on various
fields that relate to the pipe head
itself. and then a filter icon for
calibration plans that help you filter
on various fields in the calibration
plan itself. But because my list is very
small, I can easily navigate around.
It's important to note that the
calibration plans that are listed will
only be applicable for the volume of the
pipette that's in selection. So, let's go
ahead and select this pipette. And I have
a couple of options. I have an ISO
calibration plan that utilizes ISO
specifications
or I have an option to use this
userdefined calibration plan where I've
specifically defined the pass or fail
tolerances for this pipette. I'm going
to go ahead and use the ISO tolerances
from 2022.
So I've selected my pipette. I've selected
the corresponding calibration plan. I've
confirmed all of the details of the
calibration plan. And then last but not
least, I need to select the first due
date. This pipette is going to be due
today. So I'll go ahead and select okay.
Next, I'll go ahead and select a second
pipette. So this is where that master
calibration plan comes into play. I have
the second pipette that I'm actually going
to use the userdefined tolerances for.
So again, I se have my pipette selected. I
have my calibration plan selected. I'm
confirming the calibration plan details,
but this pipe head is not due until
September. So, I'm going to go ahead and
select the first due date for this pipette
and click okay.
So, again, as I mentioned, you can have
one master schedule that has all kinds
of different pipettes and calibration
plans within it, and they all have
different due dates. You can see that
I've got this pipette that has a due
date of 78, 2024
and this pipette that has a due date of
September 6th, 2024.
So once you've added or taken away
pipettes from this schedule,
you can go ahead and select the save
icon and now your schedule's in place.
So now if I head back to the home
screen, I'll see that I have one pipette
that's due and that's the pipette that I
selected that's due for today. Another
important thing to note is that if you
want to utilize the calibration label
function of our Telware and you want
those calibration labels to have the
next due date, it's very very important
that you create schedules within our
Telware. There are a lot of customers
that will not utilize the schedule
feature within our Telware because maybe
they have a master scheduling software
that controls the scheduling for all of
the items in their laboratory, not just
pipettes, but also instruments, etc.
However, again, if you want to use the
pipette calibration label within our
Telware and you want the next due date
to be listed on the label, you'll want
to create a schedule within the
application itself for all of those
pipettes. Okay, that concludes our brief
tutorial. Do you have additional
questions? Please contact us at 1
option3 or at supporticmp.com.
Thank you.
